takeaway: Hot, sticky Friday under an active Pacific moisture band: possible early coastal showers in northern Pacific Costa Rica, then mostly cloudy with scattered afternoon storms; rains can linger near the coast tonight. Surf winds stay Pacific/onshore — Papagayo is light/variable today (not glassy offshore), trending west to southwest this weekend and south–southwest early next week; early checks only. Distant East Pacific storms stay near Baja and Hawaii; a new low south of southern Mexico now has a high (~80%) chance of forming within a week. Prolonged multi-day rain remains watch-only.

periods.label: Days 1–3 (Fri–Sun)
periods.pattern: Costa Rica’s weather service says the Pacific moisture band (ITCZ) is active and favoring a humid, showery Friday — cloudiness offshore may nudge Guanacaste coasts early, then scattered afternoon showers and thunderstorms across Pacífico Norte; Nicoya heat stays sharp (around 34°C). Weekly guidance: no tropical waves crossing the next few days, with Pacific moisture holding into the weekend (early coastal rains possible; afternoon storms more widespread). Ensemble averages keep Nicoya daily rain mostly light to moderate — typical rainy-season cells, not a stuck rain machine — with some U.S. and European means a bit wetter Friday than the quieter AI-ensemble take. Official longer outlook still keeps northern Pacific on the drier-than-normal side this week (roughly 5–90 mm Pacífico Norte for 28 Sep–4 Oct). Near-surface Papagayo winds: light/variable under 5 kt today with northwest about 10 kt elsewhere; tonight light/variable Papagayo and west about 10 kt elsewhere; weekend trends southwest–west, then south–southwest by Sunday.
periods.implications: Best outdoor window is morning before scattered afternoon storms; expect sticky air and possible early coastal showers. For surf, treat Friday–Sunday as Pacific/onshore–side days: light/variable Papagayo is not glassy all-day offshore. Early checks only.
periods.confidence: High that Friday is an ITCZ / Pacific-moisture day with scattered storms and no nearby cyclone threat. Moderate on exact Nosara shower timing and how firmly weekend west/southwest onshore holds at the beach.

periods.label: Days 4–7 (Mon–Thu)
periods.pattern: Official weekly guidance expects continued humid Pacific inflow without another tropical wave in the near term, and Pacífico Norte remaining quieter than peak rainy-season weeks. Ensemble averages show continued moist Pacific-side days into early next week — often light to moderate daily totals near Nicoya — without a Costa Rica–centered rain machine. Longer official outlook keeps Pacífico Norte drier than normal into early October (next week roughly 1–70 mm). Marine winds hold south to southwest through Monday. A new East Pacific low could form south of southern Mexico late weekend / early next week and drift west-northwest away from Costa Rica.
periods.implications: Keep early-week plans flexible for quick storms. Surf-wind quality looks weaker than trade-offshore days: expect Pacific/south–southwest flow and choppier faces, with only early checks for any leftover glass. Nicaragua is not showing a clean all-day offshore signal for Nosara mornings in this window.
periods.confidence: Moderate for a quieter-than-peak Pacífico Norte theme after yesterday’s wave pulse; low–moderate on exact wet-day timing and how firmly early-week onshore winds hold.

periods.label: Days 8–15
periods.pattern: Costa Rica’s longer-range outlook keeps Pacífico Norte drier than normal from early into mid-October, with the dry signal strengthening after about October 12. No official extreme-rain event is flagged for the current week. Ensemble means still allow some moist days into mid-October, and the U.S. tropics outlook notes a chance of a broader Central American rain-gyre pattern early in its week-2 window (around Oct 7 onward) — worth watching, not a locked-in flood spell. Distant East Pacific activity remains focused near Mexico and farther west; formation odds south of southern Mexico are now high (~80%) through seven days.
periods.implications: Treat any wet day as a short cell unless a new watch develops. Outdoor and surf planning can assume the quieter Pacífico Norte lean until guidance changes; re-check midweek if a gyre signal firms up.
periods.confidence: Moderate for the quieter-than-peak theme; low for day-by-day detail and for any week-2 gyre risk past about a week.

gyreWatch.possibleTiming: No focused gyre window over Costa Rica now; yesterday’s Wave #48 was a one-day pulse, and the weekly outlook sees no tropical waves in the next few days. Broader week-2 (around Oct 7+) gyre mention in U.S. tropics guidance remains a longer-range watch only.
gyreWatch.supporting: Active Pacific moisture band is bringing humid, showery conditions Friday into the weekend. Broad moist Pacific flow remains nearby offshore. Some ensemble means keep light-to-moderate Pacific-side rain into early next week, with a few wetter days around early week-2. U.S. tropics outlook notes model support for a possible Central American gyre early in week-2. Distant East Pacific storms keep the far-Pacific moisture field active near Mexico.
gyreWatch.conflicting: No closed gyre sits over Costa Rica or Nicaragua on the main ensemble averages. Official Friday Pacífico Norte forecast is scattered afternoon showers under Pacific-moisture factors, not a multi-day washout. Weekly outlook: no tropical waves the next few days. Longer official outlook leans drier for northern Pacific into October, with no extreme event flagged for this week. Named East Pacific systems track along or well off Mexico / Hawaii, not toward Costa Rica.

surfWinds.regime: Pacific / onshore (light/variable Papagayo Fri → SW–W Sat → S–SW Sun–Mon)
surfWinds.detail: Papagayo waters: light/variable under 5 kt today with northwest about 10 kt elsewhere and scattered showers. Tonight light/variable Papagayo and west about 10 kt elsewhere. Weekend trends southwest to west about 10–15 kt, then south to southwest Sunday–Monday about 10–15 kt. Mid-level maps are mixed (U.S. ensemble means lean west–southwest near Nicoya; European means sometimes show more easterly aloft over Nicaragua) — trust the marine surface call for beach wind. Do not read Papagayo light/variable as glassy all-day offshore. Nicaragua is not offering a clear all-day offshore quality signal for Nosara this stretch.
surfWinds.bestWindows: Early checks only Friday–Monday. Expect choppier Pacific/onshore–side flow most of the day. No clean all-day offshore / Caribbean-trade signal this period.
surfWinds.confidence: High on the marine forecast trend (light/variable Papagayo today, then southwest–west weekend and south–southwest early next week). Moderate on exact hour-to-hour beach winds Friday–Saturday while Papagayo stays light/variable.

Surf winds still Pacific/onshore: light/variable Papagayo confirmed today, then clearer southwest–west this weekend and south–southwest Sunday–Monday. Genesis chance south of southern Mexico edged up to high (~80% in 7 days) from ~70% yesterday. Tropical Depression Nineteen-E is no longer listed; active systems are Hurricane Rachel (near Baja) and Tropical Storm Nolo (near Hawaii) — neither threatens Costa Rica. Prolonged-rain watch stays watch-only.
practical: Best outdoors: Friday morning before scattered afternoon storms; watch for possible early coastal showers and sticky Pacific-side humidity. For surf, treat today through early next week as Pacific/onshore — early checks only; light/variable Papagayo is not all-day glass. No tropical wave is lined up for the next few days. Prolonged multi-day rain is not the baseline.
